title: Jamaican sprint star who set all-time marks in the 100m and 200m
clues: Stands 1.95 m (6'5"), unusually tall for a 100 m champion, using a long stride to surge late in races.
Only sprinter to win both the 100 m and 200 m at three consecutive Olympics (2008, 2012, 2016).
Collected IAAF/World Athletics World Athlete of the Year honors six times across his career.
Clocked 9.58 for 100 m and 19.19 for 200 m at the 2009 World Championships in Berlin—both still-standing world records.
Nicknamed “Lightning,” famous for a celebratory “To Di World” pose seen around the globe.

title: Kenyan marathoner who twice set the official 26.2-mile world record
clues: A long-distance road racer famed for near-metronomic pacing over the marathon.
He hails from Kenya’s Rift Valley and trains with a disciplined camp in Kaptagat.
Won Olympic marathon gold in Rio 2016 and defended the title at Tokyo 2020 (held in 2021).
Completed a special exhibition marathon in Vienna in 2019 in under two hours, though not record-eligible.
Twice broke the official marathon world record in Berlin, clocking 2:01:39 (2018) and 2:01:09 (2022).

title: American swimmer famed for distance freestyle dominance and multiple world records.
clues: She burst onto the global stage by winning Olympic gold as a teenager in a distance freestyle event.
She has repeatedly lowered the long-course world records in both the 800m and 1500m freestyle.
Her early training was with Nation’s Capital Swim Club before starring at Stanford, where she won multiple NCAA titles.
She became the first swimmer to win the same individual Olympic event three Games in a row in the 800m freestyle.
A Bethesda, Maryland–born star often nicknamed the sport’s “distance queen.”

title: Kenyan middle-distance runner who set a world record in an Olympic final
clues: A two-lap specialist famed for front-running with silky, metronomic pacing.
Captured Olympic gold in his event at both London 2012 and Rio 2016.
Represents Kenya and comes from the Maasai community.
Lowered the men’s 800 m world record to 1:40.91 while winning the London 2012 final without a pacemaker.
His father, Daniel, won a 1968 Olympic silver medal in the 4x400 m relay for Kenya.

title: Venezuelan triple jump phenom with Olympic gold and multiple world titles
clues: A horizontal jumps specialist who has dominated her event on the global stage since the late 2010s.
Trains in Spain under legendary coach Iván Pedroso, known for opening rounds that put finals out of reach.
Won Olympic gold at Tokyo 2020 with an Olympic record, earning her nation’s first Olympic title in athletics.
Shattered a world record that had stood since the 1990s and later extended the indoor global mark past 15.70 meters.
Venezuelan superstar nicknamed “La Reina del Triple,” and a four-time outdoor world champion (2017, 2019, 2022, 2023).
